newsitem.title: UK: New FTSE European stock index goes live.
newsitem.headline: New FTSE European stock index goes live.

text.p: A European stock index of the 300 largest and most actively traded companies went live on Monday, against a background of record-breaking rallies this summer from Frankfurt to London.

The FTSE Eurotop 300 represents 65 percent of the total market capitalisation across the 14 European markets, according to the FTSE International, which created the index along with the Amsterdam Exchanges (AEX).

The index will allow traders and fund managers to benchmark the performance of Europe's stock markets as a whole. It will also be available as a "Euro-Block", representing the countries that are expected to be in the first wave of monetary union.
By early afternoon, the Eurotop 300 was down 7.94 points or 0.79 percent at 1,000.21.

"Today represents the first time that investors and market professionals have been able to have a meaningful measure of Europe's quoted blue chip companies as a whole," said Mark Makepeace, managing director of FTSE International.

"Come European monetary union, investors in Euro-based markets are likely to widen their core investment scope outside of their home nation and, accordingly, the ability to follow and track the European markets overall will be vital," he said.
The components of the index are Britain, Italy, the Netherlands, France, Germany, Belgium, Austria, Ireland, Norway, Denmark, Finland, Spain, Sweden and Switzerland.
